title: Keep the account right after decisions you did not make

blocks.text: You run the issuer's authorization host for a credit card programme. `Account` keeps one cardholder's account, and its `authorize` already answers the network's `0100`s. Two kinds of complaint keep reaching the call centre:

items: after a stay or a fill-up, part of what the merchant first asked for still shows as blocked, long after the final charge has posted;
after last Saturday's outage, cardholders whose purchases went through during it got further approvals afterwards, and their accounts ended up below zero once everything cleared.

blocks.text: Finish `standIn` and `clear` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Account.java`. When you're done, `ledger()` and `available()` match what each cardholder has really spent and committed to, whoever approved the purchase and whatever the clearing file says. About six lines in total.
The tests use other cards, amounts and approval codes than the lesson, including a purchase a terminal approved on its own.

cases.says: an authorized purchase cleared for the amount it was held for leaves the ledger and what is available both lower by that amount
a stand-in advice is acknowledged with an 0130 and 39=00, lowers what is available but not the ledger, and its clearing record posts it
a purchase cleared for less than was authorized costs the cardholder the cleared amount
once a purchase clears, none of its hold is left, even when the final amount is smaller
a purchase approved offline arrives only as a clearing record and is still posted, leaving other holds alone
a stand-in approval larger than what is available is still acknowledged with 00 and counted, so available goes below zero

origin.section: 7.4. A Decision Taken Elsewhere Arrives as an Advice, and the Issuer Must Apply It

concepts: A stand-in or offline approval reaches the issuer as an advice or a clearing record, and the issuer applies it as if it had approved it, even when the account goes below zero.
In the dual-message flow an approval only holds the money; the clearing record posts the final amount and releases the whole hold, and without it the hold lapses and the merchant is never paid.
